en: The Hymn to the Venerable Mahābodhi.
Om! Homage to Śākyasiṃha, the accomplished one, the renowned one, the conqueror of the immortals, the peaceful, the dispassionate, and the one of perfectly pure conduct.
I perpetually bow down to Śrī Śākyasiṃha, the Lord of the Universe and the source of all virtues. || 1 ||

I perpetually bow to the glorious Śākyasiṃha, whose head has the luster of a parasol, whose hair is excellent and dark blue, who is beautifully adorned with the *ūrṇā* tuft, who has a broad forehead, and whose large eyes have the hue of blue lotuses. (2)

I perpetually bow to the glorious Śākyasiṃha, who has a prominent nose, full cheeks, lips like the bimba fruit, and a chest like that of the king of beasts; he possesses a golden complexion with the luster of refined gold. (3)

I perpetually bow to the glorious Śākyasiṃha, whose belly is concealed by his robe, whose ears are adorned with beautiful earrings, whose cheeks are decorated with the excellent cloth of the three lines, whose arms reach down to his knees, and who resembles the trunk of an elephant. (4)

I perpetually bow to Śrī Śākyasiṃha, who is measured by men with various flowers, who is endowed with the auspicious Śrīvatsa mark and the two excellent marks, and whose body is beautified by the eighty minor characteristics. 5.

I perpetually pay homage to the Teacher, the supreme one, the hero among men, the illusory son, the compassionate Lord of Jinas, the son of Śuddhodana, the knower of the world, the Lord of Sages, the glorious Lion of the Śākyas. (6)

I perpetually bow to the Lion of the Śākyas, whose hands bear the mark of the wheel, who resembles a fresh sprout, whose gait possesses the grace of an elephant in rut, who shines resplendently, and whose pair of feet is worshipped by gods and asuras. (7)

O Śākyasiṃha, who possesses the supreme awakening capable of leading those worlds that perceive the fear of the suffering of the three types of suffering to safety; O you with the intoxicated tongue and excellent eyes, I bow to you constantly. 8.
The hymn to the venerable Mahābodhi is completed.
